blocks.content: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the last-in-first-out (LIFO) principle. That means

items: The last element added is the first to be removed from the stack.
The first element added is the last to be removed from the stack.

blocks.content: Imagine you have a pile of plates in a cafeteria.
If you add a new plate to this pile,

items: it will be the first one to be removed.

blocks.content: If you want to take the last plate,

items: you will have to remove all the plates on top.

blocks.content: Basically, the last plate added will be the first to be removed, and the first plate added to the pile will be the last to be removed.
The pile of plates is a stack as it follows the LIFO principle.
